operative_text:
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–134(c)): (1) A DEALER OR OTHER PERSON MAY NOT SELL, RENT, LOAN, OR TRANSFER A REGULATED FIREARM TO A PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE IF THE DEALER OR OTHER PERSON HAS ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE THAT THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE: (I) WAS PREVIOUSLY CONVICTED OF: 1. A CRIME OF VIOLENCE; ... OR (II) INTENDS TO USE THE REGULATED FIREARM TO: 1. COMMIT A CRIME; OR 2. CAUSE HARM TO THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, TRANSFEREE, OR RECIPIENT OR ANOTHER PERSON. (2) A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 15 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–133(b)(2)): (I) EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SUBSECTION (C) OF THIS SECTION, A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A MISDEMEANOR AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO: 1. FOR A FIRST OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 5 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH; AND 2. FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4–204(c)(1)(i)): A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and, in addition to any other penalty imposed for the crime of violence or felony, shall be sentenced: 1. FOR A FIRST OFFENSE, to imprisonment for not less than 5 years and not exceeding 20 years; AND 2. FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 10 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 20 YEARS.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 7–104(h)): (1) A PERSON CONVICTED OF THEFT OF A FIREARM, INCLUDING AN ANTIQUE FIREARM OR A REPLICA OF AN ANTIQUE FIREARM, IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND: (I) 1. FOR A FIRST CONVICTION, IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT FOR NOT LESS THAN 2 YEARS AND NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS AND A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $2,500;
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–141(b)(1)): A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and on conviction is subject to imprisonment FOR NOT LESS THAN 5 YEARS AND not exceeding 15 years AND a fine not exceeding $25,000.
Section 3 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5–142(c)): A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SECTION IS GUILTY OF A MISDEMEANOR AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH.
